payload.title: Thu 11/5: Lunch at the desk, again
payload.purpose: The workday eating pattern, without shame, and what dietary guidance in the program does with it.

captions.LI:
Eating lunch at your desk isn't a moral failing.

For many working professionals, it's just Thursday. The reality of back-to-back meetings, project deadlines, and inbox management means meals happen when they can, not always when or how we'd prefer.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance meets you where you are. We don't start with rules about when or where you should eat. We start with understanding your actual day, your actual constraints, your actual relationship with food in the context of a busy professional life.

Our registered dietitians work with clients to build sustainable patterns that fit real schedules. That might mean learning to keep satisfying options at your desk, recognizing true hunger versus stress eating during a workday, or finding small shifts that make a difference without requiring a complete life overhaul.

The program includes nutritional planning, grocery store tours, and navigating eating out. These aren't theoretical lessons. They're practical skills taught by professionals who understand that sustainable change works within your life, not against it.

Dietary guidance is one of four pillars in our intensive outpatient program, alongside behavioral therapy, culinary classes, and mindful movement. One program, not four. Available both onsite in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Most health insurance plans cover the program under mental health benefits, and patients typically attend for little to no cost.

bariatriccounselingcenter.com

#BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Tue 11/10: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI: When your patients are on weight loss medications, the behavioral half of the equation is just as critical as the pharmaceutical. The Bariatric Counseling Center provides the comprehensive behavioral support that helps patients build the habits that sustain their results, group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education. One program, not four. The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. We accept most health insurances; our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits. payload.title: Mon 11/23: What intuitive eating means here
payload.purpose: Intuitive Eating as taught in the program, with a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians in the room.

captions.FB:
Intuitive eating is a core part of the work we do at the Bariatric Counseling Center.

It's not eating whatever you want whenever you want. It's learning to recognize hunger and fullness cues, understand emotional triggers, and make intentional choices without rigidity or shame.

In our program, intuitive eating is taught by a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians working together in the same room. You get the behavioral tools and the nutrition education at the same time, so the concepts connect.

We serve people who struggle with weight loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic overeating. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Link in the first comment.
